name: KQL - Kibana Query Language Fundamentals
description: Kibana Query Language (KQL) syntax for querying Elastic SIEM data. Used in Discover and Dashboard visualizations to hunt events, filter data, and build detection rules.
source: CDSA Module 02: Security Monitoring & SIEM Fundamentals
notes:
KQL runs at http://<TARGET_IP>:5601 → Discover (or Dashboard filter bar).

Basic syntax:
  field:value                           exact match
  field: value1 OR value2              multiple values same field
  field:value1 AND field2:value2       both conditions
  NOT field:value  or  field:!value    negation
  field: prefix*                       wildcard
  field:>5  field:>=5  field:<5        comparison (numeric)
  @timestamp >= "2023-03-03T00:00:00.000Z"  timestamp range

Important field types:
  event.code        → Windows event ID (ECS preferred)
  winlog.event_id   → Windows event ID (Winlogbeat specific)
  user.name         → username (use user.name: not user.name.keyword in KQL)
  user.name.keyword → use .keyword variant for aggregations/visualizations
  host.hostname     → host reporting the event
  @timestamp        → event timestamp
  winlog.logon.type → logon type (Interactive, RemoteInteractive, Network...)
  winlog.event_data.SubStatus → failure reason sub-code
  winlog.channel    → Security, System, Application, etc.
  event.action      → action string (e.g. 'logged-on', 'logoff')
  group.name        → group name (local group membership events)
  related.ip        → IPs involved in the event

Useful SubStatus values for event 4625 (failed logon):
  0xC0000072 → Account disabled
  0xC000006A → Wrong password
  0xC0000064 → Username does not exist
  0xC0000234 → Account locked out
